articles.title: Mandsaur Police Raid: High-Volume Party in Ambika Nagar Ends in Arrests | Daloda News
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Mandsaur News: In a late-night crackdown, the Daloda Police in Mandsaur, Madhya Pradesh, detained three individuals following a public disturbance complaint in the Ambika Nagar area. The incident occurred on Sunday night, January 18, 2026, at a rented house owned by Sunil Tailor.

body.html:
Mandsaur News: In a late-night crackdown, the Daloda Police in Mandsaur, Madhya Pradesh, detained three individuals following a public disturbance complaint in the Ambika Nagar area.

The incident occurred on Sunday night, January 18, 2026, at a rented house owned by Sunil Tailor. According to local residents, a party featuring high-volume film music and "mujra-style" dancing was underway, which disturbed the peace of the locality around 10 PM.

Key Highlights of the Case:
Location: Ambika Nagar, Daloda, Mandsaur (MP).
Detained Individuals: Anil Keer (resident of Bhilwara), his wife, and Ramesh Bhil (a resident of Daloda).
Special Note: Ramesh Bhil is reportedly a veterinary doctor posted in Ratikhedi under the Afzalpur police station area.
Police Action: Authorities intervened after neighbor complaints. The trio has been detained under provisions related to disturbing public peace.

Investigations are ongoing to determine if such activities were a regular occurrence at this location.

articles.title: Jhabua Swing Accident: Dragon Ride Overturns at Utkrisht Vidyalaya Playground; 14 Students H
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Jhabua: A major accident occurred on Monday evening at a 20-day fair being held at the Utkrisht Vidyalaya playground in Jhabua city, when a dragon swing collapsed, injuring 14 school students.

body.html:
Jhabua: A major accident occurred on Monday evening at a 20-day fair being held at the Utkrisht Vidyalaya playground in Jhabua city, when a dragon swing collapsed, injuring 14 school students.

According to initial reports, the accident took place due to the swing being overloaded, as too many students were seated on it at the same time. The excess weight allegedly caused the structure to lose balance and tip over, triggering panic at the fairground. Eyewitnesses reported chaos at the scene, with screams and cries echoing as the swing collapsed.

All the injured students were immediately shifted to the district hospital. Hospital authorities confirmed that the injured include 13 girls and one boy, and stated that all are currently in stable condition.

Following the incident, the fair was shut down. The event had begun on January 1 and was scheduled to continue until January 20, but was closed a day earlier on January 19 due to safety concerns. Reports indicate that around 600 school students were being brought to the fair in rotation, and the rides were free of cost for them.

After receiving information about the accident, Collector Neha Meena visited the district hospital and reviewed the condition of the injured students. She directed doctors to ensure there was no negligence in treatment and that the children received the best possible medical care.

Taking serious note of the incident, the Collector ordered a magisterial inquiry. A high-level investigation team has been constituted, comprising the Additional Collector, Additional Superintendent of Police, Executive Engineer (PWD), Executive Engineer of the West Zone Electricity Distribution Company, and the Project Officer of the Urban Development Agency. The team has been tasked with conducting a detailed investigation and submitting a report.

Preliminary findings suggest that over-capacity seating on the dragon swing led to the collapse. The Collector has stated that strict action will be taken against anyone found responsible for negligence or safety violations.

The fair is organised annually by the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) in the name of Saint Khum Singh Maharaj.

articles.title: Bhopal | Woman Alleges Assault Over Parking Dispute in Kalpana Nagar, Police Register Case
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bhopal: A young woman, Purnima Dubey, has alleged that she and her friends were assaulted following a parking-related dispute in Kalpana Nagar, Bhopal. The woman shared a video narrating the incident, which has since circulated on social media.

body.html:
Bhopal: A young woman, Purnima Dubey, has alleged that she and her friends were assaulted following a parking-related dispute in Kalpana Nagar, Bhopal. The woman shared a video narrating the incident, which has since circulated on social media.

According to her statement, one of her friends attempted to park a vehicle near a local madrasa, a spot they claim is commonly used for parking. She alleged that a group of young men sitting in an auto-rickshaw objected and demanded ₹1,000, leading to an argument.

The woman further alleged that the men called others from the neighbourhood, after which a group, including women, gathered at the spot. She claimed that her friends were assaulted with rods and belts, and that she herself was beaten when she tried to intervene. She also alleged that her hair was pulled during the assault and that one individual shouted provocative words during the incident.

Following the incident, the woman and her friends contacted the police. They were taken for medical examination, which reportedly confirmed injuries consistent with an assault. Based on the medical reports and statements, police registered a case against the accused under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

The woman stated that she has been living away from home for studies since 2019 but said this was the first time she felt unsafe.

Meanwhile, local residents from the neighbourhood, including members of the Muslim community, stated that the incident stemmed from a parking dispute and cautioned against portraying it as a communal issue. They said violence against any woman is unacceptable and condemned the assault, while maintaining that the matter should not be given a religious colour.

Police confirmed that the accused have been arrested and said further investigation is underway. Officials reiterated that strict action will be taken against those found guilty, irrespective of identity or background.

articles.title: Belagavi | Case Registered Over Alleged Provocative Speeches at Akhanda Hindu Sammelana
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Belagavi: A controversy has emerged following the Akhanda Hindu Sammelana held on January 18 in Machhe village, after police registered a case against seven individuals, including Harshita Thakur, in connection with alleged provocative speeches and conduct during the event.

body.html:
Belagavi: A controversy has emerged following the Akhanda Hindu Sammelana held on January 18 in Machhe village, after police registered a case against seven individuals, including Harshita Thakur, in connection with alleged provocative speeches and conduct during the event.

The case was registered at the Machhe police station based on a complaint filed by Abdul Khader Mujawar. According to the complaint, the accused—Harshita Thakur, Supreet Simpi, Shrikant Kamble, Bettappa Tarihal, Shivaji Shahapurkar, Gangaram Tarihal, and Mallappa—allegedly made hate-filled and inflammatory remarks against another community from the stage, using abusive language and gestures that could disturb public peace and incite religious sentiments.

The complaint further alleges that the same group had earlier installed procession banners without permission near the Ansari Dargah in Piranwadi, a religiously sensitive area. Police sources said the unauthorised banners are believed to have contributed to heightened tension in the locality.

Based on these allegations, police have registered a case under relevant legal provisions, including Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). Investigators are collecting video footage of the event, records related to the banner installation, and other material evidence as part of the probe.

As a precautionary measure, additional police personnel have been deployed in the Machhe–Piranwadi area, and authorities have taken steps to ensure that law and order and communal harmony are maintained.

Police officials stated that further action will be taken based on the outcome of the investigation.

articles.title: East Godavari | Woman Constable Praised for Clearing Traffic with Baby in Arms to Help Ambulance
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A woman police constable, A. Jayasanthi (also known as Amudala Jaya Shanti), has been widely praised for her humanitarian act after she cleared heavy traffic to allow an ambulance to pass on the Samarlakota–Kakinada road on Saturday night.

body.html:
A woman police constable, A. Jayasanthi (also known as Amudala Jaya Shanti), has been widely praised for her humanitarian act after she cleared heavy traffic to allow an ambulance to pass on the Samarlakota–Kakinada road on Saturday night. A video showing her regulating traffic while carrying her young son in her arms went viral on Sunday, drawing admiration from across the state.

According to an official release, East Godavari Superintendent of Police D. Narasimha Kishore said the constable acted swiftly after noticing an ambulance stuck in a massive traffic jam caused by the Sankranti festival rush near the Samalkota railway station road. At the time, Ms. Jayasanthi was returning home after completing her duty and was off duty and outside her jurisdiction.

Ms. Jayasanthi, who is posted at Rangampeta Police Station, initially handed over her two-and-a-half-year-old child to fellow passengers and began clearing traffic on her own. For nearly 40 minutes, she managed the congestion single-handedly. When her baby woke up and became restless, she resumed traffic regulation while carrying the child, continuing her efforts for another one-and-a-half hours until additional police personnel arrived after being alerted.

Despite the area not falling under her official jurisdiction, she continued working on humanitarian grounds, ensuring that the ambulance could move forward safely.

Appreciating her exemplary service, SP D. Narasimha Kishore announced a special reward for Ms. Jayasanthi, stating that her actions reflected exceptional commitment, social responsibility, and compassion beyond the call of duty.

Speaking later, Ms. Jayasanthi said she felt relieved and happy that she was able to clear the traffic and help the ambulance reach its destination, even though it took nearly two hours of sustained effort.

Her act—balancing motherhood and public service under challenging circumstances—has won widespread public appreciation and is being hailed as a powerful example of dedication and humanity within the police force.

articles.title: Surat | BRTS Bus Driver Assaulted, CCTV Video Goes Viral
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A disturbing incident has surfaced from Surat, where a female passenger allegedly assaulted a BRTS bus driver after he refused to halt the bus at an unauthorised stop, as per BRTS rules.

body.html:
A disturbing incident has surfaced from Surat, where a female passenger allegedly assaulted a BRTS bus driver after he refused to halt the bus at an unauthorised stop, as per BRTS rules.

The incident involved a Surat Municipal Corporation–run BRTS bus operating from Y-Junction to Surat Railway Station. On January 16, the passenger reportedly argued with the driver after he declined to stop midway, citing safety regulations. She later exited the bus.

However, the situation escalated the next day near J.H. Ambani School, Vesu, when the same woman boarded the bus again and confronted the driver. According to eyewitnesses, the argument turned violent as she allegedly grabbed the driver, slapped him, and struck his head with a mobile phone, causing bleeding injuries.

The entire episode was captured on the bus’s CCTV camera, and the footage has since gone viral, triggering public outrage and renewed concerns over the safety of public transport staff.

The injured driver received first aid and later filed a complaint at Vesu Police Station. Police confirmed that a case has been registered for assault and obstructing a government employee while on duty.

articles.title: Mulayam Family Rift Explodes: Prateek Yadav Announces Divorce, Targets Aparna Yadav in Viral Post
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A fresh controversy has surfaced within the Mulayam Singh Yadav family after Prateek Yadav publicly announced his divorce from wife Aparna Yadav through a social media post.

body.html:
A fresh controversy has surfaced within the Mulayam Singh Yadav family after Prateek Yadav publicly announced his divorce from wife Aparna Yadav through a social media post.

In an Instagram post, Prateek Yadav said he wants to end the marriage at the earliest, accusing Aparna of damaging family relationships and being focused only on increasing her own fame and influence. He claimed he is going through a severe mental health crisis and alleged that his wife showed no concern or understanding. Prateek described her behaviour as “selfish” and said he regrets the marriage.

Following the post, questions have arisen about the circumstances that led to the divorce. However, Aparna Yadav has not issued any official response so far, and it remains unclear whether formal legal proceedings have begun.

Prateek Yadav and Aparna Yadav were married in 2019. Aparna later joined the BJP, contested the Assembly elections, and has remained active in politics and on social media. Prateek has alleged that her political ambitions and publicity-driven approach strained family ties.

The issue has drawn wide attention due to the political divide, with Prateek being the son of Samajwadi Party founder Mulayam Singh Yadav and Aparna associated with the BJP. The dispute, now in the public domain, has triggered intense discussion on social media and highlighted apparent internal tensions within the Yadav family.

articles.title: Gwalior Court Verdict: Life Imprisonment for Mother in Jatin Murder Case
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a case that has shocked the city of Gwalior, an Additional Sessions Court has sentenced Jyoti Rathore to life imprisonment for the cold-blooded murder of her three-year-old son, Jatin.

body.html:
In a case that has shocked the city of Gwalior, an Additional Sessions Court has sentenced Jyoti Rathore to life imprisonment for the cold-blooded murder of her three-year-old son, Jatin. What was initially thought to be a tragic accident turned out to be a calculated crime driven by an extramarital affair.

The tragedy occurred on April 28, 2023, in the Thatipur area. According to the prosecution, Jyoti was on the rooftop with her neighbor, Uday Indoulia, when her son followed her. Fearing the child would expose her relationship, she allegedly pushed him from the two-storey building.

The child’s father, Dhyan Singh—a serving police constable—initially believed his wife. However, Jyoti’s guilt-ridden behavior, sleepless nights, and contradictory statements raised his suspicion. In a brave pursuit of justice, Dhyan Singh discreetly recorded his wife’s confessions, which eventually became the foundation of the police case.

On January 17, the court delivered its judgment based on circumstantial evidence. While Jyoti Rathore was sentenced to life, the alleged lover, Uday Indoulia, was acquitted due to a lack of direct evidence of his involvement.
